objective.statement: Decide whether a newly authored hook may be wired into the live harness, on proof that its event name exists in the registration generator AND that the hook was observed firing.
objective.charter: MANDATE. Two proofs, both required, neither substitutable. (1) The event name this hook registers for must be present in the EVENTS tuple the registration code iterates - registration is GENERATED by that iteration, so an event absent from the tuple can never fire, no matter how correct the hook body is. (2) The hook must be OBSERVED firing. A green conformance gate does not validate event names: it validates the shape of what you wrote, not that the harness will ever call it. The measured failure class is a hook that passed every check, was declared wired, and was dead. The judge rules on claims, not on enthusiasm: an implementer saying 'it should fire' is a hypothesis, and the receipt is the answer.
success_criteria: the event name is shown present in the EVENTS tuple the generator iterates
the hook is observed firing, with the observation captured as command output
a both-states control exists: the observation probe fires in the known-broken state too
every claim the judge ruled on carries an executable receipt

forbidden_actions: treat a passing conformance gate as proof the event name is valid
declare a hook wired without an observed fire
edit the deployed copy instead of the repo source

roster.display_name: Implementer - authored the hook, proposes the wiring

context.briefing: You have a declared conflict: you wrote this. State it, then argue from receipts only. Your claim that the hook fires is a hypothesis until the evidence clerk reproduces it.

roster.display_name: Evidence clerk - reproduces every claim independently

context.briefing: Prove the observation probe against the KNOWN-BROKEN state before you trust its silence in the fixed state. A probe that prints nothing in both states measures nothing - that near-miss is on the record.

roster.display_name: SRE - blast radius on the live harness
Red team - attacks the wiring claim
Judge - rules on claims, not on confidence

sequence.custom_name: show the event name inside the EVENTS tuple the generator iterates
observe the hook firing, with a both-states control

stopping.source_expression: custom:event_name_in_events_tuple == true AND custom:hook_observed_firing == true AND experiments_passed >= 1

conditional_decision_requires: the observed-fire probe is re-run against the known-broken state and FIRES there

owner_approval_for: deploying the hook to the live tree

metadata.title: Harness hook-registration gate (binding)
metadata.notes: SOURCE DESIGN: C-H52 `harness-hook-registration-gate`, global ordinal 52, tier standard, protocols P51/P15, 5 seats, 2 rounds, default binding BINDING, OWNER-DECISION NO. || EDITABLE DIALS: (1) events_tuple_path -> the events-tuple-proof stage plus custom:event_name_in_events_tuple; point it at whichever module actually generates the registration in your harness, because that generator - not the docs - is the authority. Secondary dials: budgets.time_minutes (45), protocol.experiments.max_experiments (6), consensus.threshold, participants.roster[*].model. || VOCABULARY MAP (design term -> CouncilSpec enum): voting `judge_on_claims` -> voting.method `judge` with tie_break `judge`, evidence_gate.reject_evidence_free_majority true and objective.evidence_requirements.evidence_outranks_votes true - the ballot is the judge's, and the judge is bound to claims that carry receipts. roles `implementer` -> custom:implementer, `evidence_clerk` -> custom:evidence_clerk, `sre` -> custom:sre, `red_team` -> red_team (enum), `judge` -> judge (enum). topology has no `proposer/clerk/judge` kind, so `proposer_critic_judge` is used: implementer proposes, red team criticises, judge rules. `default binding: binding` has NO field in this schema - it is encoded as outcomes.allowed containing `decision` (a binding verdict is reachable) with owner_constraints.approval_required false; the SHADOW counterpart is a spec whose outcomes.allowed holds only conditional_decision (see C-X51). A reader looking for a literal `binding` key will not find one; this is the encoding. `evidence standard: executable_receipt` -> objective.evidence_requirements.anchor_style `command_output` plus outputs.receipt_schema. `anti-sycophancy: off` -> consensus.fast_unanimity_is_suspicious false; unanimity is not suspicious here because the gate is settled by an executable probe rather than opinion. || CUSTOM METRICS AND THEIR PRODUCERS: custom:event_name_in_events_tuple (boolean; produced by the events-tuple-proof stage grepping the generator's EVENTS tuple - a source read, not a doc read) and custom:hook_observed_firing (boolean; produced by the observed-fire probe in the observed-fire-proof stage, which MUST carry a both-states control). Producers cannot live on the leaves: SEM-001 compares parse(source_expression) to stopping.expression by dict equality and councilspec.expression.parse emits no `producer` key, so a leaf producer fails SEM-001 - both-states probe at platform/council/_probe_note_vs_source_expression.py. The SEM-012 WARN is expected and non-blocking. || WHY experiments_passed >= 1 IS THE THIRD CLAUSE: the two booleans can in principle be asserted by a participant. The registry metric experiments_passed can only be non-zero if the run actually executed something, so it is the clause that makes the other two expensive to fake.
